metric_identity.metric_name: AI Labor Market Impact and Job Displacement: Net Job Creation Projections 2025-2030
metric_identity.source_report: World Economic Forum Future of Jobs Report 2025
metric_identity.methodology_notes: WEF surveyed 1,000+ leading global employers collectively representing 14M+ workers across 22 industry clusters and 55 economies. Survey administered May-August 2024, capturing employer forecasts for 2025-2030. ILO (International Labour Organization) employment data used to translate fractional net growth forecasts per role into absolute job creation/displacement estimates. Supplemented by partner data from ADP, Coursera, Indeed, and LinkedIn. Respondents included Chief People Officers, Chief Learning Officers, Chief Strategy Officers, and CEOs. The report builds on methodology from previous editions (2016, 2018, 2020, 2023) with refined and new questions. Cross-referenced with Goldman Sachs (2023), IMF (January 2024), OECD Employment Outlook (2023-2025), and McKinsey Global Institute research.

metric_value.value: +170 million jobs created, -92 million jobs displaced = net +78 million jobs by 2030 (WEF). Job disruption equates to 22% of total employment by 2030. 41% of employers plan to reduce workforce as AI automates tasks. AI and data processing alone: +11M created, -9M displaced.
metric_value.unit: count (millions of jobs); percentage (of total employment)
metric_value.comparison_baseline: WEF 2020 report projected +97M created, -85M displaced = net +12M by 2025. Goldman Sachs (March 2023): 300M full-time job equivalents exposed to automation globally. IMF (January 2024): ~40% of global employment exposed to AI (60% in advanced economies, 40% in emerging markets, 26% in low-income countries). OECD: 27-28% of jobs in OECD countries at high risk of automation. McKinsey (November 2025): 57% of US work hours technically automatable with existing technologies. 14% of workers self-report already having been displaced by AI as of 2025.
metric_value.market_layer: cross-cutting (labor market impact spans all AI value chain layers)

trend.year_over_year_change: Net job creation projections grew from +12M (2020 report, 2020-2025 horizon) to +78M (2025 report, 2025-2030 horizon), reflecting both higher creation and higher displacement estimates. In H1 2025, ~78,000 tech job losses were directly attributed to AI. 48% of US employers (vs 41% global average) plan workforce reductions due to AI, indicating acceleration in advanced economies.
trend.forecast_value: By 2030: fastest-growing roles include big data specialists, AI/ML specialists, fintech engineers, software developers, security management specialists. Fastest-declining: postal service clerks, bank tellers, cashiers, data entry clerks, administrative assistants, and newly: graphic designers and legal secretaries. Digital access expected to create 19M jobs and replace 9M by 2030. Green transition projected to create 34M additional jobs by 2030. 77% of companies plan to reskill workers 2025-2030. 39% of existing workforce skills expected to become outdated by 2030.
trend.velocity_indicator: adoption_doubling_time: AI adoption among surveyed employers growing rapidly, with 86% of companies expecting AI to transform their business by 2030. Goldman Sachs projects AI transition unemployment increase of +0.5 percentage points (transitory). Graphic designers and legal secretaries appeared in fastest-declining list for the first time in the 2025 edition, signaling generative AI's accelerating impact on knowledge work.

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: The WEF's net +78M jobs figure is the most widely cited macro-level statistic on AI's labor market impact and is essential context for any AI startup pitch or business plan. For entrepreneurs, the key insight is that AI is not simply eliminating jobs but restructuring the labor market: 170M new roles require new skills, products, and services. The 41% of employers planning workforce reductions represents a massive demand signal for automation tools, workflow optimization platforms, and AI-augmented productivity software. Simultaneously, the 77% planning to reskill/upskill workers creates a parallel market for corporate training, skills assessment, and workforce transformation platforms. The appearance of graphic designers and legal secretaries in the fastest-declining list for the first time signals that generative AI is now impacting knowledge workers, not just routine tasks, opening opportunities for AI-powered creative and legal tools. The IMF's warning that 60% of advanced-economy jobs are AI-exposed but only half will benefit means there is a large segment of workers who need augmentation tools to remain productive. For European entrepreneurs specifically, the WEF data shows the green transition creating 34M new jobs by 2030, presenting a dual opportunity at the intersection of AI and sustainability. The Goldman Sachs estimate that AI could boost global GDP by 7% over 10 years provides the macroeconomic justification for AI investment that reassures investors despite displacement concerns.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Build products targeting the 'displacement-to-reskilling' pipeline: 92M workers will need new skills or new roles. Enterprise upskilling platforms, AI-assisted career transition tools, and skills verification systems are high-growth segments. For B2B SaaS founders: the 41% of employers planning workforce reductions are actively seeking automation and AI workflow tools now. Frame product positioning around 'augmentation' rather than 'replacement' to align with corporate messaging (77% plan reskilling, not just layoffs). The fastest-growing roles list (big data, AI/ML, fintech, cybersecurity) signals where to build and where to hire.

confidence.cross_reference: WEF Future of Jobs Report 2025 (primary: 1,000+ employers, 55 economies). Goldman Sachs 'The Potentially Large Effects of AI on Economic Growth' (March 2023): 300M jobs exposed. IMF Staff Discussion Note (January 2024): 40% global employment exposed. OECD Employment Outlook 2023-2025: 27-28% OECD jobs at high automation risk. McKinsey Global Institute (November 2025): 57% of US work hours automatable. LinkedIn Work Change Report (January 2026): 1.3M new AI jobs created 2023-2025. St. Louis Federal Reserve (August 2025): 0.47 correlation between AI exposure and unemployment increases. Brookings Institution: study on US workers' capacity to adapt to AI displacement. All major sources agree that AI will cause significant labor market restructuring, though estimates of scale vary depending on definition of 'affected' vs 'displaced' vs 'exposed'.
confidence.caveats: The +78M net figure is based on employer forecasts, not observed outcomes, and employers historically overestimate both creation and displacement. The WEF's previous 2020 report projected +12M net by 2025, but ex-post verification is limited. The 170M/92M split measures structural shifts over 5 years and does not account for frictional unemployment or transition periods where displaced workers have not yet found new roles. The 41% workforce reduction figure reflects employer intent, not actual layoffs. Goldman Sachs' 300M figure measures 'exposure' (tasks that could theoretically be automated), not jobs that will be eliminated. The IMF's 40% figure similarly measures 'exposure' not 'displacement'. Generative AI's impact on knowledge work (graphic designers, legal secretaries) is a very recent phenomenon and projections carry higher uncertainty. Regional variation is significant: 48% of US employers plan reductions vs 41% globally, suggesting advanced economies face faster disruption. The 'net positive' framing (+78M) may mask severe distributional effects: gains accrue to different workers, sectors, and geographies than losses.
